BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION

 IN THE MATTER OF SOUTHWESTERN                            )
 PUBLIC SERVICE COMPANY’S                                 )
 APPLICATION FOR: (1) REVISION OF ITS                     )
 RETAIL RATES UNDER ADVICE NOTICE                         )   DOCKET No. 25-00079-UT
 341; AND (2) OTHER ASSOCIATED RELIEF.                    )
                                                          )
 SOUTHWESTERN PUBLIC SERVICE                              )
 COMPANY, APPLICANT                                       )

                                    PROTECTIVE ORDER

       THIS MATTER comes before Patrick Schaefer, Hearing Examiner for the New Mexico

Public Regulation Commission, upon Southwestern Public Service Company’s Verified Motion

for Entry of Protective Order, filed February 18, 2026. The Hearing Examiner FINDS and

CONCLUDES as follows:

       1.      SPS’s Motion states that during discovery parties may seek documents and other

information that may contain confidential or proprietary information that should not be publicly

disclosed. SPS states that issuance of a protective order will permit parties to respond to future

requests for confidential or proprietary information without the delay caused by seeking a

protective order at the time each request seeking confidential or proprietary information is issued.

       2.      Referencing NMSA 1978, §§ 14-2-1(F) and (L), and 62-6-17(C), SPS requests a

Protective Order to be able to provide certain Confidential Material (as defined below) to parties

herein pursuant to Confidentiality Agreements with those parties.

       3.      The Inspection of Public Records Act 1 (IPRA) declares that “[e]very person has a

right to inspect public records in this state” except as provided by law. The statute defines the

term “public records” (disclosure of which is required unless an exception applies) broadly to

include not only records created by or required to be kept by an agency, but also any other


   1
       NMSA 1978, §§ 14-2-1 to -12 (2024).
                      BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Protective Order                                                 Docket No. 25-00079-UT


documents “received, maintained or held by or on behalf of any public body [that] relate to public

business.” 2 IPRA stands for the principle that, in New Mexico, “[t]he citizen’s right to know is

the rule and secrecy is the exception.” 3

        4.       The policy of the Commission, as defined by 1.2.2.8(A) NMAC, is to allow full

and complete access to public records in accordance with IPRA.

        5.       Notwithstanding the requirements of IPRA, the Commission’s administrative rules

provide for the protection of parties who may be adversely affected by public disclosure of

confidential or proprietary information and trade secrets. Specifically, 1.2.2.8(A) and (B) NMAC

authorize the Commission’s designated hearing examiners to enter appropriate protective orders

to prevent public disclosure of confidential or proprietary information as well as protectable trade

secrets. 4

        6.       The Commission has previously entered protective orders in proceedings when

requested by applicants.

        7.       SPS’s requests a protective order in this case to establish the conditions for

disclosure and use of confidential and proprietary information.




    2
        NMSA 1978, § 14-2-6(G).
    3
          State ex rel. Newsome v. Alarid, 1977-NMSC-076, ¶ 34, 568 P.2d 1236, superseded on other grounds
by statute as stated in Republican Party of N.M. v. N.M. Taxation & Revenue Dep’t, 2012-NMSC-026, ¶¶14-16,
283 P.3d 853. See also § 14-2-5 (providing that “[r]ecognizing that a representative government is dependent
upon an informed electorate, the intent of the legislature … is to ensure, and it is declared to be the public policy
of this state, that all persons are entitled to the greatest possible information regarding the affairs of government
and the official acts of public officers and employees”).
    4
         These rules are based in part on IPRA itself, see NMSA 1978, § 14-2-1 (2024), as well as the “office,
books, and records” provision of the Public Utility Act. See NMSA 1978, § 62-6-17(C) (1993). This latter
provision is not directly applicable to telecommunications service providers but is nevertheless instructive with
respect to the interpretation of the Commission’s rules.

                                                       -2-
                       BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Protective Order                                                  Docket No. 25-00079-UT


       8.      The Motion states that SPS “sought the positions of the parties, and no party who

responded opposed the motion.” 5

       9.      SPS has established a sufficient basis for the granting of a protective order.

   IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED:

       A.      SPS’s motion for a protective order is GRANTED.

       B.      This order establishes a procedure for the handling of information that a party

claims is confidential material. This order shall not be construed as a ruling on the confidentiality

of any document or information.

       C.      Consistent with IPRA and the statutory limits on the Commission’s authority to

issue protective orders, parties SHALL ONLY seek protection of material that is protectable under

statute and regulation, SHALL NOT designate documents as confidential that are not entitled to

protection, and SHALL NOT make blanket assertions that all documents or entire subsets of

documents in this case are subject to protection.

       D.      Designating Information as Confidential

               1.        This order provides protection for confidential and proprietary information

       identified and clearly designated by parties as “CONFIDENTIAL MATERIAL.”

               2.        Material may only be designated as confidential if the disclosing party can

       establish that the material is not in the public domain and is protected by applicable law,

       including IPRA and the New Mexico Trade Secrets Act. No material shall be treated as

       confidential material if it: (a) is in the public domain at the time of disclosure; (b) becomes

       part of the public domain through no fault of a party who received it under this order; (c)




   5
       Motion at 3.

                                                 -3-
                     BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Protective Order                                                Docket No. 25-00079-UT


       is in the lawful possession of the receiving party at the time it is disclosed under this order;

       (d) is or has been received by a party on a nonrestricted basis from a third party that has

       the right to make such a disclosure; or (e) has been or becomes disclosed as non-

       confidential material in any other legal or regulatory proceeding.

               3.      All material submitted to the Commission as provided below or furnished

       to other parties pursuant to any request for information, subpoena, or other mode of

       discovery that is claimed to be of a trade secret, proprietary or confidential nature, and

       protectable under IPRA shall be clearly designated “CONFIDENTIAL MATERIAL” by

       the party claiming protection.

               4.      If a document contains both confidential and non-confidential information,

       the party claiming confidentiality shall claim protection only for the portions of the

       document that satisfy the standards for confidential treatment and clearly identify the

       specific portions of the document for which confidentiality is claimed.

       E.      Segregation of Files

               1.      Access to and review of confidential material shall be strictly controlled by

       the terms of this order.

               2.      Any document containing confidential material should be watermarked or

       otherwise clearly reflect that it contains confidential material.

               3.      Confidential material provided IN RESPONSE TO DISCOVERY

       REQUESTS SHALL NOT be “filed” with the Commission.

               4.      Confidential material to be filed with the Commission shall be marked

       CONFIDENTIAL and filed electronically as confidential.




                                                -4-
                      BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Protective Order                                                 Docket No. 25-00079-UT


               5.        Confidential material filed with the Commission shall be e-mailed to the

       Hearing Examiner and the subject line and text of the e-mail shall make clear that the

       message is intended to transmit confidential material in this docket. The materials will be

       withheld from inspection by any person except under the conditions established in this

       order unless the parties agree the material may be released for public review or, after notice

       to the parties and hearing, by order of the Commission and/or a court with jurisdiction to

       order public disclosure.

       F.      Confidentiality Agreement

       No access to confidential material shall be authorized under the terms of this order until

the person requesting access to the material signs a confidentiality agreement in the form attached

to this order as Attachment A. The executed confidentiality agreement shall be filed with the

Commission and served on the parties as required by 1.2.2.10 NMAC and applicable orders in this

case prior to inspection of the confidential material. Commissioners and their advisory staff and

expert consultants, Commission’s Records Management Bureau, Commission’s General Counsel

and staff, Hearing Examiners and staff, and court reporter, are not required to sign the

confidentiality agreement to view confidential material.

       G.          Availability to the Commission and Parties

       Except as otherwise provided in this order, the only persons permitted access to the

confidential material (other than the individuals identified in the preceding paragraph) are parties

to this case and their employees and legal counsel who have executed the confidentiality

agreement.

       H.      Availability to Non-Signatories




                                                -5-
                      BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Protective Order                                                 Docket No. 25-00079-UT


         All persons who receive service of filings in this case and who have not executed the

confidentiality agreement shall receive, on the date that they are filed, the affidavits required under

paragraphs L(1)(e) and L(2)(b) and all non-confidential portions of any documents marked as

confidential material in redacted form.

         I.     Preservation of Confidentiality

         Persons provided access to confidential material by operation of this order shall not use or

disclose the confidential material for purposes of business or competition or any other purpose

other than the purpose of preparation for and adjudication of this proceeding (except as provided

in paragraph P) and any appeals arising from this proceeding. Confidential material shall be used

only as contemplated here and parties shall take all reasonable precautions to keep the confidential

material secure. The contents of the confidential material shall not be disclosed to anyone other

than persons who have executed the confidentiality agreement.

         J.     Challenges to Claims of Confidentiality

         A party may at any time challenge a claim that materials identified as confidential should,

in fact, be given confidential status. In the event of such a challenge, the following procedures

apply:

                1.      The party asserting the challenge shall contact counsel for the party holding

         the allegedly confidential materials and attempt to resolve any differences informally.

                2.      If the parties cannot resolve the disagreement informally, then the party

         challenging the claim of confidentiality shall file a motion with the Commission for a ruling

         on the challenge (a process referred to as a “request for confidentiality determination”).

                3.      When a request for confidentiality determination is filed and served, the

         owner or holder of the material held out as confidential shall, within three business days of


                                                 -6-
                     BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Protective Order                                                Docket No. 25-00079-UT


       service of the request for confidentiality determination, e-mail the materials to the Hearing

       Examiner for in-camera inspection. The documents should comply with the formatting

       requirements described in ordering paragraph E of this document.

               4.      The holder of the materials held out as confidential shall, without order or

       action by the Commission and within five business days after service of a request for

       confidentiality determination, file an initial brief and supporting affidavit stating in detail

       the basis for the claim of confidentiality and may request a hearing on the matter. Failure

       to file an initial brief and supporting affidavit shall be deemed a waiver of the

       confidentiality claim.

               5.      Within five business days after service of the initial brief and supporting

       affidavit, the party that filed the request for confidentiality determination shall file a

       response brief and supporting responsive affidavit.

               6.      Within three business days of service of the response brief and supporting

       affidavit, the holder of the purportedly confidential material may file a reply brief.

               7.      Any other party may brief its position by filing a brief opposing the claim

       of confidentiality five business days after service of the initial brief or supporting

       confidentiality and non-disclosure by filing a brief within three business days after service

       of the response of the party that filed the request for confidentiality determination.

               8.      The burden of proof to show the confidentiality of the materials held out as

       confidential rests with the party claiming confidentiality.

               9.      The parties shall not make public any information regarding materials held

       out as confidential until the Commission rules on the claim of confidentiality. Following




                                                -7-
                     BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Protective Order                                                Docket No. 25-00079-UT


       a Commission ruling on confidentiality, the information shall be made available only

       pursuant to the Commission’s order(s).

       K.      Requests Not to Disclose to Persons Signing a Confidentiality Agreement

       If any party possessing confidential materials wishes to decline to provide those materials

to specific parties who have signed confidentiality agreements, then the party possessing the

materials must file a pleading with the Commission prior to the time the material is due to be

produced explaining the reasons why the materials should not be provided. The party denied

access to the confidential materials may then file a response within five business days of service

of the possessor’s pleading. The party seeking to preclude parties from receiving confidential

materials shall have the burden of proof. Confidential material shall not be produced to the

challenged party until a ruling by the Hearing Examiner.

       L.      Use of Confidential Materials and Bench Requests

               1.      Use by Staff and parties.

               If any party other than the party asserting the claim of confidentiality intends to use

       confidential material or material over which a claim of confidentiality is made in this

       proceeding in pre-filed testimony (including exhibits) or at the hearing, and even if the

       party using the confidential material does not intend to challenge the claim of

       confidentiality, then the following procedures shall apply:

                       a.     The party intending to use the confidential material shall inform the

               party asserting the claim of confidentiality of the intent and manner of use as

               follows: (i) for use in pre-filed testimony (including exhibits), notice to be filed on

               the date the testimony is filed, and (ii) for use at the hearing, notice to be provided




                                                -8-
                    BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Protective Order                                               Docket No. 25-00079-UT


               to the Hearing Examiner and parties and Staff as early as is feasible and preferably

               to be filed before the start of the hearing unless otherwise ordered or approved.

                      b.          Within three business days of receiving notice of the intent to use

               confidential material in pre-filed testimony or within two business days of receiving

               notice of the intent to use confidential material at the hearing, the party claiming

               confidentiality shall state whether it objects to public disclosure of the confidential

               material. If the party asserting confidentiality fails to make this statement, its

               objection to disclosure shall be waived.

                      c.          Pending a ruling on confidentiality, any party using confidential

               material in pre-filed testimony (including exhibits) shall, on the date that the notice

               is filed: (i) file a public version with the Confidential Material redacted; (ii) file a

               confidential version in accordance with the procedure in Paragraph E; and (iii)

               serve the confidential version on parties who have signed the confidentiality

               agreement and to the Hearing Examiner.

                      d.          If the party asserting the confidentiality of material objects to public

               disclosure of the material, it shall file a request seeking confidential treatment of

               the material within three business days after it receives notice of the intended use

               of the material in pre-filed testimony or within two business days after it receives

               notice of the intended use of the material at the hearing.

                      e.       Any request filed pursuant to Paragraph L(1)(d) shall include:

                             i.           An affidavit consistent with 1.2.2.8.B(1) NMAC that

                      satisfies the claimant’s burden of making a prima facie showing that

                      protection is appropriate for the information claimed to be confidential


                                                   -9-
                    BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Protective Order                                               Docket No. 25-00079-UT


                      material and that includes (at a minimum) the following information with

                      respect to each document marked confidential:

                                     (1)     the date that the material was prepared;

                                     (2)     the author of the material;

                                     (3)     a list of all persons (other than the disclosing party

                                     and its representatives) in possession of the material;

                                     (4)     a description of the subject matter of the material and

                                     the contents of the material;

                                     (6)     the number of pages of material;

                                     (7)     how the material was acquired; and

                                     (8)     the basis for all claims of confidentiality, including a

                                     showing that each document marked confidential comes

                                     within one or more of the exceptions to the general

                                     disclosure requirement of IPRA.

                            ii.      A brief that sets forth the legal basis for protection and states

                      whether the public interest requires that the material be used and whether

                      an abstract of or the extraction of specific information from the material can

                      be used as an alternative.

                      f.      The party asserting the confidentiality of the material shall e-mail

               the Hearing Examiner the confidential materials for in-camera inspection.

                      g.      Within seven days of the filing of a request under Paragraph L(1)(d),

               the party seeking to use the confidential material shall file a response addressing

               the legal and factual merits of each confidentiality claim, including Staff’s or the


                                              - 10 -
                     BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Protective Order                                                Docket No. 25-00079-UT


               party’s position on whether the confidential material is in fact confidential. Any

               factual assertions in the response shall be supported by a verifying affidavit.

               2.      Use by party asserting confidentiality.

               If any party asserting the confidentiality of material intends to use the material in

       this proceeding in pre-filed testimony (including exhibits) or at the hearing, then the

       following procedures apply:

                       a.     The party shall file a notice of intent that describes the manner of

               use and requesting confidential treatment of its use of the material as follows: (i)

               for use in pre-filed testimony (including exhibits), notice to be filed on the date the

               testimony is filed; and (ii) for use at the hearing, notice to be provided to the

               Hearing Examiner and parties and Staff as early as is feasible and preferably before

               the start of the hearing. Pending a ruling on confidentiality, the party using

               confidential material in pre-filed testimony (including exhibits) shall, on the date

               that the notice is filed: (i) file a public version with the confidential material

               redacted; (ii) file a confidential version under seal in accordance with the procedure

               in Paragraph E; and (iii) serve the confidential version on parties who have signed

               the Confidentiality Agreement and the Hearing Examiner.

                       b.     Such party shall file a request seeking confidential treatment of the

               material on the date that the notice required under Paragraph L(2)(a) is filed. This

               request shall include the affidavit and brief described in Paragraph L(1)(e).

                       c.     Within seven days of filing a request under Paragraph L(2)(b), or as

               otherwise ordered, Staff shall, and any other intervener may file a response

               addressing the legal and factual merits of each confidentiality claim including


                                               - 11 -
                     BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Protective Order                                                Docket No. 25-00079-UT


               Staff’s or the party’s position on whether the material is in fact confidential. Any

               factual assertions in the response shall be supported by a verifying affidavit.

               3.      Bench Requests

               If the Hearing Examiner or Commission requires a party to file a document and the

       party objects to public disclosure of the document or portions of the document on

       confidentiality grounds, then the following procedures apply:

                       a.     On or before the deadline for filing the document, the party shall (i)

               file a public version of the document with the confidential material redacted; (ii)

               file a confidential version of the document in accordance with the procedure in

               Paragraph E; and (iii) serve the confidential version on parties who have signed the

               confidentiality agreement and the Hearing Examiner.

                       b.     On or before the deadline for filing the document, the party shall file

               a request seeking confidential treatment of the material, including the affidavit and

               brief described in Paragraph L(1)(e).

                       c.     Within seven days of the filing of the request seeking confidential

               treatment of the material, or as otherwise ordered, Staff shall, and any intervenor

               may, file a response addressing the legal and factual merits of each confidentiality

               claim including Staff’s or the party’s position on whether the material is in fact

               confidential. Any factual assertions in the response shall be supported by a

               verifying affidavit.

               4.      Rulings

                       a.     The Commission shall evaluate the materiality and relevance of the

               confidential material to this case and, if necessary, determine if claimed


                                               - 12 -
                     BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Protective Order                                                Docket No. 25-00079-UT


               confidential material contains confidential or proprietary information and, if so,

               determine whether the public interest requires that the confidential or proprietary

               information be produced at the hearing in this case, whether an abstract of or the

               extraction of specific information from the confidential or proprietary information

               should be produced for use at the hearing, or whether the Confidential Material

               shall be admitted and treated as a confidential exhibit.

                        b.    The Commission may issue a ruling on the requests under this

               paragraph based upon the affidavits and/or a hearing or other procedure as

               determined by the Commission. The confidential material shall remain confidential

               pending a ruling by the Commission.            Following a Commission ruling on

               confidentiality, the information shall be available only as provided by Commission

               order.

                        c.    Following a Commission ruling on confidentiality or privilege, the

               information shall be made available only pursuant to the Commission’s Order;

               provided however that an application for reconsideration, rehearing or interlocutory

               appeal filed by any holder of confidential material shall act as a stay of such order

               pending reconsideration, rehearing or interlocutory appeal.

               5.       Hearings involving Confidential Material

               During this proceeding, those portions of any hearings where confidential material

       obtained pursuant to the terms of this order are likely to be disclosed shall be conducted in

       a manner that the Commission determines is consistent with the Open Meetings Act, IPRA,

       the Public Utility Act, and other relevant statutes.

               6.       Admissibility


                                               - 13 -
                      BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Protective Order                                                 Docket No. 25-00079-UT


               The parties retain the right to object to the admission into evidence of any

       confidential material on any proper grounds including relevance or materiality.

       M.      Filing and Delivery Pursuant to Commission Electronic Filing Policy

       Whenever the terms of this order require a filing of pleadings or materials, such filings are

subject to the Commission’s Electronic Filing Policy then in effect. Service of the filed documents

shall be made to parties having filed confidentiality agreements by emailing scanned versions of

the materials reflecting the formatting identified in ordering paragraph E. To the extent that this

order requires delivery of any materials to the Commission in connection with a request for

confidentiality determination, delivery to the Hearing Examiner will be by email as an attachment

or as electronic file transfer. The email delivering the document shall briefly describe the materials

and reflect the formatting directions at ordering paragraph E but shall not include any commentary

or argument. Notice of the delivery of materials to the Hearing Examiner will be provided to all

parties and individuals on the service list.

       N.      Appeal

       Sealed portions of the record in the proceeding may be forwarded to any court of competent

jurisdiction for purposes of an appeal.

       O.          Continuation of Protection

       Disclosure of confidential material is limited by this order for two years from the date of

the final order or final decision on appeal whichever is later, provided that the Commission may

extend the period of protection upon a motion of a party filed prior to expiration of the period of

protection.

       P.      Use in Other Commission Proceedings




                                                - 14 -
                    BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Protective Order                                               Docket No. 25-00079-UT


        Nothing in this order prohibits a person who executes a confidentiality agreement from

seeking to use confidential material in other Commission proceedings, subject to any applicable

rulings in such proceedings, and provided the original owner or holder of the material is served

with the notice of intent to use the material. The procedure set forth in Paragraph L(1) shall apply.

        Q.     For purposes of this order, “Commission” means presiding officer, Hearing

Examiner, or the Commissioners.

        R.     The provisions of 1.2.2.8(B) NMAC governing the procedures to be used when any

person desires to protect documents or information from disclosure are waived pursuant to

1.2.2.8(D) NMAC.

        S.     Any person executing a confidentiality agreement consents to the jurisdiction of the

Commission and the New Mexico courts for resolution of disputes regarding alleged violations of

this Order.

        T.     This order is effective immediately.

        U.     A copy of this Order shall be served on all persons on the official service list.

        ISSUED under the seal of the Commission at Santa Fe, New Mexico, on February 24,

2026.
